title: The Aged Sufferer Waited Long
description: The Aged Sufferer Waited Long in Tonic Solfa to ALL SAINTS, NEW, doh is Bb: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 3 verses and a piano.
about: Stephen Greenleaf Bulfinch wrote these words. They were printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion, compiled by Samuel Longfellow and Samuel Johnson (Boston, 1848), as hymn 116, “The Pool of Bethesda”.

The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Metre Double (8.6.8.6.8.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to ALL SAINTS, NEW; any other Common Metre Double tune fits them as well.
underlay: The aged suf-fer-er wait-ed long Up-on Be-thes-da's brink; Till hopes, once ris-ing warm and strong, Be-gan in fears to sink; And hea-vy were the sighs he drew, And fer-vent was his prayer, For he, with safe-ty full in view, Still lan-guished help-less there.

lines: Till hopes, once rising warm and strong,
And heavy were the sighs he drew,
For he, with safety full in view,
His hope grew dim; but one was nigh
That gentle voice, that pitying eye,
Each pang that human weakness knows
He spake, and lo! the sick arose,
With grief and pain we lie,
And, longing for Thy heavenly rest,
O, may the Saviour's words of peace
Bid every doubt and suffering cease,

source: A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848)
licence: Public domain: Stephen Greenleaf Bulfinch died in 1870.
credits: Words by Stephen Greenleaf Bulfinch (1809–1870), public domain, as printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848); set to ALL SAINTS, NEW by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
